transcript.content: Hello. I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Dr. Smith. Well, I suppose I'm here because I'm just... I'm at the end of my rope, honestly. For over a year now—fourteen months, actually, if we want to be exact, ever since the Q3 rollout last year—I’ve been trying to get someone, anyone really, to take what's happening to me seriously. 

I work as a computer support specialist, so I know how these backend systems operate. I have a degree in this, I've been doing it for decades. But they brought in this new ticket rotation system at work, and they paired it with these new, supposedly "random" security audits. And I know exactly what they are doing. They are using these systems to build a massive paper trail against me. I mean, the way the routing works now, the most complex, unresolvable tickets just happen to land in my queue right before the deadline. And then, like clockwork, a security audit hits my specific terminal to check my compliance. 

I’ve brought this up to management, I've sat down in meetings with them, and they just keep pulling up these system logs, pointing at the screen, and telling me that it's just the new policy, that the algorithm is randomized, and that it affects everyone on the floor. But I look at the timestamps, I see the routing protocols, and it’s obvious to anyone who actually knows how to read the data. I even started keeping my own spreadsheets at home to track the frequency of the audits on my workstation compared to the rest of the team because it’s so blatantly targeted. It’s incredibly stressful when you know you’re being systematically set up to be fired, and management just keeps smiling and hiding behind these logs. So... yeah, I guess that's why I'm here. It's just wearing me down, trying to get people to see what's right in front of them.
Aside from the suspicion regarding your workplace, have you been hearing, seeing, or sensing things that others around you do not seem to notice?

Hearing or seeing things? No, no, nothing like that. I know exactly what you’re getting at—you’re asking if I’m hallucinating, if the stress of this whole ordeal has got me hearing voices or seeing shadows in the corner of my eye. I assure you, my mind is perfectly sound, and my senses are sharp. I mean, I had my hearing checked just a couple of years ago, and my vision is fine—well, I use bifocals now, obviously, at my age, but when you spend eight to ten hours a day staring at dual monitors, you make sure to keep your prescription updated. But no, there are no phantom sounds or visions. Absolutely not. 

The only thing I’m seeing that others aren't—or, more accurately, that others are deliberately choosing to ignore—are the actual, concrete data points. The raw logs. It’s not some trick of the mind, Dr. Smith, it’s right there in the system architecture. When I pull the routing tables from the Tuesday morning shift and compare them to the Thursday afternoon audit schedule, I’m not seeing things that aren't there, I'm just reading the SQL output. Anyone with a basic understanding of database management could see it if they just sat down and actually looked at the spreadsheets I've put together. 

So, no, no voices, no visions. Just the facts. And that's what makes this whole situation so incredibly frustrating, you see? Because they try to make me feel like I'm the one who's losing it, like I'm just making it all up out of thin air, when all I'm doing is pointing at the screen and saying, 'Look at the timestamp! Look at the IP address of the audit trigger!' It's all just... it's right there. I don't need to imagine anything when the evidence is sitting in my outbox.
